resources.title: What Is Concentrated Liquidity, and What Does It Fragment?
resources.tldr: Capital efficiency comes at the cost of scattering LP funds across ranges. Clear on both halves, which most explanations of this are not.

resources.title: Shared Liquidity Explained
resources.tldr: One wallet balance backing several positions at once. A different answer to fragmentation than concentration, and worth understanding alongside it.

resources.title: The Clarity Act and Open-Source Developers
resources.tldr: A legal officer arguing for rules rather than against regulation, with specific attention to who is liable for publishing code. Short and unusually direct.

resources.title: Wake Debugging Guide
resources.tldr: Console logging, Python fuzzing, ipdb integration and profiling for Solidity. Practical tooling detail of a kind that rarely gets written down.

resources.title: Omnipair Oracle-Less Lending: Audit Summary
resources.tldr: A published audit of a lending design that deliberately avoids oracles. Reading the findings is the fastest way to see what that choice costs elsewhere.

resources.title: What Teams Found Using Wake Arena on Production Code
resources.tldr: Feedback from LUKSO, Monerium and IPOR after running the tooling against live contracts. Useful for what it says about where automated review still misses.

resources.title: Anthropic Can Now Crack Smart Contracts: What AI Agents Mean for Web3 Security
resources.tldr: Models finding real contract vulnerabilities changes who can attack and how cheaply. Thinks through what that does to the economics of auditing rather than just noting it happened.

resources.title: Agentic AML: AI Agents in Anti-Money-Laundering Compliance
resources.tldr: Compliance teams drown in alerts that are mostly false positives. Covers where agents genuinely reduce that load and where handing them the decision would be reckless.

resources.title: Building a Blockchain Investigation AI Agent
resources.tldr: Tracing funds across mixers and bridges is slow, repetitive work that suits an agent well. A practical look at what such an investigation loop actually needs.

resources.title: 2022: A Year of Progress and a Decade of Maturation
resources.tldr: A custodian's retrospective on the year the credit chain collapsed, written from the position of holding other people's assets through it.

resources.title: 2023: The Flight to Safety and the Path Forward
resources.tldr: What institutional clients did after the previous year's failures. The behavioural shift toward regulated custody is the substance here.

resources.title: 2021 in Hindsight
resources.tldr: The peak year reassessed with several years of distance. Retrospectives written long after the fact are more useful than the commentary published at the time.

resources.title: DAO Governance That Actually Works
resources.tldr: One token one vote collapses in practice, and this covers the structures teams reach for instead. Grounded in mechanisms rather than governance theory.

resources.title: Token Compliance: MiCA, the Howey Test, and Launching Safely
resources.tldr: Two regimes with different questions, applied to the same token. Structured around not walking into a securities problem rather than around what the law says.

resources.title: Real-World Assets Onchain: Tokenising Beyond the Hype
resources.tldr: Separates what is genuinely live in tokenised finance from what is still being promised, then sits with the custody and legal questions nobody has closed.

resources.title: ERC-3643: A Compliance-Focused Protocol for RWA Tokenization
resources.tldr: A token standard with identity verification and transfer restrictions built in, rather than enforced by the interface. Explains what that moves onchain and why it matters.

resources.title: Tokenizing Private Markets: Venture, PE and Secondaries
resources.tldr: Private markets are illiquid by construction, not by accident. Works through which of those constraints tokenisation actually removes and which it merely relocates.

resources.title: AI Agents Handling RWA Portfolios
resources.tldr: Speculative but grounded: what an autonomous system managing tokenised real-world assets would need to be trusted with, and which of those pieces exist yet.

resources.title: Why Instant Crypto Exchanges Became a Money Laundering Hotspot
resources.tldr: Swapping without an account is convenient for everyone, including people moving stolen funds. Explains the structural reason these services attract that flow.

resources.title: Real-Time Threat Detection on Solana
resources.tldr: Extending live transaction monitoring to a chain with very different execution timing. Useful for what it implies about how little room there is to react.

resources.title: Blocking the ParaSpace Attack and Rescuing $5M
resources.tldr: An attack detected and stopped mid-flight rather than analysed afterwards. The response window here was minutes, which is the whole argument for live monitoring.

resources.title: Counter-Exploiting an Attacker's Contract: The Platypus Case
resources.tldr: Turning the attacker's own contract against them to recover funds. Legally and ethically contested, technically fascinating, and documented here in full.

resources.title: Hacking Back to Rescue Funds in the Transit Swap Attack
resources.tldr: Another live intervention, smaller in value but the same pattern. Read alongside the others it becomes a study of what defenders can actually do mid-incident.

resources.title: Choosing a Web3 Domain: Picking a Memorable Name
resources.tldr: Naming advice that mostly predates crypto but applies cleanly to it, plus the extension question that has no equivalent in traditional domains.

resources.title: Buying Your First Web3 Domain: A Step-by-Step Guide
resources.tldr: Walks a first purchase end to end. Worth reading for the part people miss, which is what you actually own afterwards and where that record lives.

resources.title: The LIBRA Playbook: How One Cluster Drained $87 Million in an Hour
resources.tldr: A single presidential tweet, a Solana memecoin, and a connected cluster of wallets that extracted $87M before most people had read the post. Forensics rather than commentary.

resources.title: Who Is the Whale Behind SHIB?
resources.tldr: Traces one wallet from a $10K trade in 2020 to over $4B at the peak. A good demonstration of how much a public ledger reveals once you follow it properly.

resources.title: What Is a Datachain?
resources.tldr: A layer one whose consensus pays miners to store data rather than to order transactions. Explains what changes when storage becomes the thing being secured.

resources.title: How Does Irys Store Data?
resources.tldr: Data held many times over by miners who have staked something, then challenged continuously to prove they still hold it. Unusually concrete about the mechanism.

resources.title: What Is Programmable Data?
resources.tldr: Data a contract can read mid-execution as a trusted input, rather than data that merely sits somewhere permanent. A meaningful distinction, argued properly.

resources.title: Cairo Scores Big With Starknet Devs
resources.tldr: Developer feedback after the move from Cairo Zero to Cairo. Worth reading as a record of what a breaking language transition feels like from the outside.

resources.title: Cairo Community Update
resources.tldr: A progress round-up spanning the editor tooling, test runner, CLI and package manager. Reads as a snapshot of a language ecosystem being assembled in public.

resources.title: Why a Linux-Based Execution Layer Changes What DeFi Can Build
resources.tldr: Argues the EVM imposes a structural ceiling, and that running a real Linux runtime onchain lifts it. Makes the constraint concrete rather than gesturing at scalability.

resources.title: Fraud Proofs, Agentic Dev Tooling and Emergency Withdrawals
resources.tldr: A monthly engineering recap, worth reading for the fraud-proof and emergency-withdrawal work. Both are the parts of a rollup that only matter when something breaks.

resources.title: Why Blockchain Benchmarks Are Usually Deceiving
resources.tldr: Every chain advertises a TPS figure and almost none of them mean the same thing. Takes apart how the number is produced and what it conceals.

resources.title: Relay Chain: A Case Study in Product-Centric Chain Architecture
resources.tldr: An interoperability product that reached 100M+ transactions, examined for what it built its own chain around. Concrete answer to when a product should become a chain.

resources.title: Turning Crypto Narratives Into Structured Agent Data
resources.tldr: Agents choke on raw feeds and scattered timelines. This is about the unglamorous work of shaping that into something a model can reason over.

resources.title: Web3 Data Access Built for AI Agents
resources.tldr: What it takes to make onchain data queryable by something that is not a human writing SQL. A good look at where the two fields actually meet.

resources.title: An Outlook on How Blockchain Will Reshape Real Estate
resources.tldr: Two and a half thousand words on where tokenisation meets an industry built on registries, deeds and jurisdictions. Ambitious, and clear about the obstacles.

resources.title: Creating More Primitives for Real Estate in DeFi
resources.tldr: Once a property is a token it can be collateral, be lent against, or sit in a pool. Works through which of those actually make sense.

resources.title: The Evolution of Web3 Gamification: From Farming to Growth
resources.tldr: Quest campaigns trained users to farm rewards and leave. Honest about why that failed and what rewarding contribution instead would require.

resources.title: Crypto Trends in 2026: Regulation, AI and Real-World Adoption
resources.tldr: A survey piece, but a well-organised one covering stablecoins, tokenised assets and institutional flows. Useful for orientation rather than depth.

resources.title: Best RPC Node Providers for Developers, Reviewed and Ranked
resources.tldr: Five providers compared on uptime, chain coverage and free tiers. RPC choice is one of those decisions made casually and regretted at scale.

resources.title: Zapper Alternatives: Free Crypto Portfolio Trackers
resources.tldr: Written because Zapper shut down in August 2026, and notable for verifying each alternative was still alive that week rather than recycling an old list.

resources.title: Inside the Jail Channel
resources.tldr: A moderator writing honestly about handling bad actors in token-gated communities. Governance as it actually happens, rather than as it is theorised.

resources.title: We Are Always Looking for Our People
resources.tldr: Six years and ten million verified wallets, reflected on by a founder. A rare piece of writing about what community infrastructure feels like to run.

resources.title: Colyseus 0.17: Reconnection, Type Safety and defineServer()
resources.tldr: A release note worth reading as design commentary. Automatic reconnection and end-to-end TypeScript safety are exactly the things multiplayer servers usually leave to you.

resources.title: Two Open-Source Multiplayer Demos: Realtime and Turn-Based
resources.tldr: One server driving clients in Unity, Godot, GameMaker, Defold, React and Three.js. The clearest demonstration of what engine-agnostic actually means in practice.

resources.title: First-Class Vite Integration
resources.tldr: Hot module reloading and unified builds for a multiplayer server. Small in scope but it removes the slowest part of the game-dev feedback loop.

resources.title: A Lesson in Brand Equity: Pudgy Penguins
resources.tldr: How one NFT collection turned a picture into a brand with retail distribution. The most instructive case in the space for anyone thinking about durability.

resources.title: The Hype Behind $TRUMP: A Marketing Analysis
resources.tldr: Treats a memecoin launch as a distribution campaign and measures it as one. Detached enough to be useful whatever you think of the subject.

resources.title: Understanding and Preventing Reentrancy Attacks
resources.tldr: The DAO hack is a decade old and the pattern still ships. Explains the mechanism properly, then the coding practices that actually close it rather than the ones people cite.

resources.title: How to Read a Smart Contract Audit Report
resources.tldr: Severity ratings, the red flags that matter, and how to check a report is genuine before trusting it. Most people who cite audits have never read one closely.

resources.title: What Is Formal Verification in Smart Contract Auditing?
resources.tldr: Proving code behaves correctly under every possible input, rather than the inputs someone thought to test. Clear on where that is worth the cost and where it is not.

resources.title: Nitron Exploit: Recovery, Restitution and Next Steps
resources.tldr: What happens after the incident report, when a team has to decide who gets made whole and how. That part is rarely documented at all.

resources.title: Updating the Liquidation Process
resources.tldr: Changing liquidation rules after community pushback, with the reasoning shown. Liquidation design decides who absorbs losses in a crisis.

resources.title: An Introduction to Force Inclusion
resources.tldr: Layer twos are fast and cheap right up until the sequencer decides not to include you. Force inclusion is the escape hatch, and this explains how it actually works.

resources.title: Working With Solana Tokens Using Native Rust
resources.tldr: Two thousand words of token handling without Anchor. Doing it the hard way once teaches you what the framework was hiding.

resources.title: Using Arweave for AI Provenance
resources.tldr: Permanent storage as a way of proving what a model was given and when. Timely, given how much of the internet is now output nobody can trace.

resources.title: The Fall of A7A5: How Sanctions Strangled a Ruble Stablecoin
resources.tldr: Coordinated US, UK and EU action enforced through chain analysis, told as a narrative. One of the clearest accounts of sanctions actually working onchain.

resources.title: Building MAS AML/CFT Expectations Into Your Controls
resources.tldr: Turns a regulator's stated expectations into repeatable, auditable controls. The gap between what a rule says and what an auditor will accept is the whole subject.

resources.title: How Credit Unions Can Identify Their Crypto Exposure
resources.tldr: You can carry crypto exposure without ever offering a crypto product, through members and counterparties. Sets out where it hides and how to measure it.

resources.title: Calculating Unrealized Gains and Losses on Solana
resources.tldr: Accounting for positions you have not closed, which is where onchain bookkeeping gets genuinely hard. Practical rather than conceptual.

resources.title: Automating Payroll Payments on Solana
resources.tldr: Paying people on a schedule from onchain funds, with the failure modes that come with it. One of the more concrete treasury operations pieces around.

resources.title: Calculating Gas Expense on Solana
resources.tldr: Fees are small individually and material at volume, and few teams track them properly until an accountant asks. This is how to actually count them.

resources.title: Redeeming 20% of TVL Without Lengthening Ethereum's Exit Queue
resources.tldr: Nearly a fifth of deposits withdrawn in 33 days while keeping the pressure off a shared queue every validator depends on. A rare account of a stress event handled well.

resources.title: Non-Custodial and Actively Defended
resources.tldr: When an exploit lands the window to prevent loss is seconds, so this describes defence designed around that constraint rather than around audits.

resources.title: Safe Staking, From Doctrine to Code
resources.tldr: Turning stated risk principles into the actual implementation, written just after the protocol had been tested by industry-wide redemptions.

resources.title: Ethereum Rich List: Where Capital Really Resides
resources.tldr: Aggregating holdings by USD value rather than by token changes the picture considerably. The first half of a two-part look at concentration.

resources.title: Ethereum Rich List: How Capital Moves and Where Risks Emerge
resources.tldr: The follow-up, tracking movement between those holders over time. Concentration is one thing; correlated movement is the part that matters for risk.

resources.title: 90% of Tokens Deployed on Uniswap v2 on Base Were Hard Rug Pulls
resources.tldr: Not an estimate but a measurement across deployments, showing scam tokens are being mass-produced rather than hand-crafted. The ratio is the finding.

resources.title: A Decade of Sanctions-Linked Exposure on Ethereum
resources.tldr: Billions moved through addresses tied to sanctions over ten years, traced. Short, and blunt about why compliance screening stopped being optional.

resources.title: 1,000+ Scan Nodes: Inside an Incentivized Detection Network
resources.tldr: How a threat-detection network pays independent operators to run scanners. Interesting as a design problem: how do you reward finding nothing?

resources.title: Invariant Testing
resources.tldr: Instead of asserting what one call returns, you state what must always hold and let the fuzzer attack it. Covers handler patterns and ghost variables, which is where this gets hard.

resources.title: Debugging Transactions
resources.tldr: Replaying a failed mainnet transaction locally and stepping through the trace is the fastest route from "it reverted" to knowing which call reverted and why.

resources.title: Code Coverage
resources.tldr: Generating LCOV output and per-test attribution, so you can see which test actually exercised a branch rather than trusting one aggregate percentage.

resources.title: What Galactic Geckos Is
resources.tldr: The premise, four factions, the artist, supply and sister collections, laid out plainly. Straight answers to the questions a collection page usually leaves you guessing at.

resources.title: Protect Your Gecko
resources.tldr: Revoking permissions you granted months ago and forgot, settling your storage setup once instead of drifting, and the frauds aimed at this community specifically.

resources.title: Buy a Gecko
resources.tldr: Five numbered steps from no wallet at all to owning one, including the thing to do the moment it arrives. A model of how onboarding docs should read.

resources.title: A Deep Dive Into DePIN
resources.tldr: Crowdsourcing storage, compute and connectivity through token incentives. Long enough to get past the acronym and into whether the economics hold.

resources.title: Beyond Hyperledger: Why Banks Are Leaving Closed Networks
resources.tldr: The permissioned-chain era in banking, and what pushed institutions toward open architectures instead. A quieter shift than the headlines suggest.

resources.title: CDK Erigon and the Limits of Rollup Infrastructure
resources.tldr: Building a chain stack on top of an existing execution client rather than from scratch. Useful for understanding what a chain deployment actually inherits.

resources.title: What Happens When Oracles Think Twice: Permissionless Oracle Design
resources.tldr: Lending protocols live or die on what they believe assets are worth. Works through designing that layer so anyone can add a feed without endangering everyone.

resources.title: The End of Looping
resources.tldr: A protocol admitting the strategy it became famous for was never the right way to take leverage. Rare candour, and the reasoning is the interesting part.

resources.title: Reclaiming Composability: DeFi's Most Underused Advantage
resources.tldr: Composability gets cited constantly and exercised rarely. Argues what would have to change for protocols to genuinely build on each other.

resources.title: Where Do the Returns Come From?
resources.tldr: Yield explained as stablecoin payment fees rather than lending or interest. Any protocol willing to answer this question plainly is worth reading on it.

resources.title: Risks and Risk Reduction
resources.tldr: What the protocol deliberately avoids doing, and which safeguards keep funds off its own balance sheet. Notable for stating the risks rather than the mitigations first.

resources.title: The Security Lifecycle of Meme Coins
resources.tldr: Follows a meme coin from deployment through listing to collapse, marking where each risk appears. The lifecycle framing makes the pattern legible.

resources.title: Token Issuance Trends Across Solana, Base and BNB
resources.tldr: Comparative data on how many tokens each chain is producing and what share is malicious. Useful for calibrating how different those ecosystems actually are.

resources.title: Giving AI Agents Security Intelligence
resources.tldr: Wiring token-risk data into an agent framework so an autonomous trader can refuse a malicious contract. An early answer to who checks what agents buy.

resources.title: Bank Frick Strengthens $1B Crypto Custody
resources.tldr: An audit of a bank's key ceremony, which is the moment custody is either done properly or quietly compromised for years. Rare visibility into that process.

resources.title: Hardening Critical CBDC Pilot Infrastructure
resources.tldr: Risks found across validator nodes and APIs during a central bank digital currency pilot. Useful for seeing how a state-run chain differs in threat model.

resources.title: Securing Privacy-Preserving Infrastructure for Institutional Adoption
resources.tldr: Reviewing a chain built so institutions can transact without publishing their positions. The privacy requirement changes what an auditor is even looking for.

resources.title: Private Cross-Chain Payments With Zashi CrossPay
resources.tldr: Shielded payments that settle across chains rather than staying inside one privacy pool. The interesting problem is keeping the privacy through the hop.

resources.title: Shielded Withdrawals Arrive on a Major Exchange
resources.tldr: An exchange letting users withdraw into a shielded address rather than a transparent one. A meaningful precedent for whether privacy survives contact with regulated venues.

resources.title: Hotels and Casinos Monetising Wi-Fi They Already Built
resources.tldr: Two decades of hospitality Wi-Fi buildout now being resold as carrier offload. The clearest example yet of decentralised infrastructure meeting an existing asset.

resources.title: The Case for Clear Rules Under the CLARITY Act
resources.tldr: How regulatory ambiguity stalls buildout, argued from the position of a network that has to deploy physical hardware to survive.

resources.title: Solving a Waterfront Connectivity Dead Zone
resources.tldr: A city closing a coverage gap using existing Wi-Fi rather than new towers, now carrying 2,000 daily users. Municipal deployment, described concretely.

resources.title: Gröbner Bases in Cryptanalysis: The Underlying Algebra
resources.tldr: Nearly ten thousand words building the machinery from scratch: polynomial rings, ideals, monomial orderings, Buchberger's algorithm. Genuinely a textbook chapter, not a blog post.

resources.title: The Exploit Is the Disclosure
resources.tldr: In Web3 an exploit is public the moment it lands, so it starts a race to copy rather than to patch. Backed by turning twelve live exploits into a study of that race.

resources.title: Encrypted Vector Databases Without Sacrificing Search
resources.tldr: Embedding attacks, and why an encryption scheme that preserves exact distances gives the game away. Deep, technical, and relevant well beyond crypto.

resources.title: What Is a Liquidity Pool? Crypto Liquidity Explained
resources.tldr: Covers pools and automated market makers, then the question most guides skip: when adding liquidity is actually the wrong move for your token.

resources.title: How to Create a Crypto Token, SPL or ERC-20
resources.tldr: The same task on Solana and Ethereum side by side, which makes the differences between the two token models unusually easy to see.

resources.title: How to Create an ERC-20 Token on Base
resources.tldr: A short deployment walkthrough that continues past minting into adding liquidity, which is where most token guides stop and most launches fail.

resources.title: Introducing Smart Loops for Leveraged Staked ETH
resources.tldr: Automating the borrow-and-restake loop people otherwise run by hand, badly. The automation is the product; the leverage is just what it enables.

resources.title: Rebuilding a Yield Product on Morpho
resources.tldr: Migrating a live strategy onto different lending infrastructure without disrupting holders. The migration mechanics are the useful part.

resources.title: Refundable Launchpads: When Sold Out Can Mean $0
resources.tldr: A project can announce millions raised and reach listing day with nothing for liquidity, because the sale was refundable. A trap worth understanding before you use one.

resources.title: Web3 Funding: Pre-Seed and Seed Report
resources.tldr: Verified deals with real medians rather than announced numbers: $5.2M seed, $2.5M pre-seed. Also covers how SAFE and token-warrant terms are currently structured.

resources.title: AI Seed Rounds: 7 Hidden Truths Founders Must Know
resources.tldr: Record funding totals hid the fact that seed rounds got harder for most teams. Seven investor patterns behind that split, with the data underneath.

resources.title: Forecasting Geopolitical Risk With Foresight Learning
resources.tldr: A small open model trained only on public news beats GPT-5 at predicting military strikes. The result matters less than the method, which is reproducible.

resources.title: AI Reaches Human Superforecaster Range
resources.tldr: On ForecastBench the best systems now sit statistically level with the median human superforecaster. Short, with the benchmark caveats stated rather than buried.

resources.title: Predicting Patient Outcomes From Clinical Notes
resources.tldr: A small model trained on existing hospital notes, with no manual labelling, predicting ventilation and dialysis. A useful counterexample to the idea that scale is the only lever.

resources.title: What Is the Internet Backbone?
resources.tldr: Submarine cables, tier hierarchies and exchange points, explained properly. Almost nobody building distributed systems knows what the packets physically cross.

resources.title: IPv8 and What Comes After IPv4 and IPv6
resources.tldr: A draft proposing 64-bit addresses with backward compatibility. Speculative, and a good excuse to understand why the previous transition took decades.

resources.title: Jobs, CPI and Fed Minutes: Two Weeks of Catalysts
resources.tldr: A macro brief written for people whose positions react to it. Shaped as a sequence of scheduled events rather than a single forecast, which is the honest way to frame it.

resources.title: Trading With the House's Money: The Funded Trader Model
resources.tldr: Trade the firm's capital and keep most of the upside. An old proprietary-trading structure arriving in crypto, and worth understanding before you enter one.

resources.title: Can Strategy Become the World's Largest Company?
resources.tldr: Works through the mechanics of the most-watched corporate Bitcoin position in public markets: how the leverage is structured and what would unwind it.

resources.title: How H100 Group Became Europe's Second-Largest Corporate Bitcoin Holder
resources.tldr: 3,506 BTC on a European balance sheet, and the financing that got it there. A concrete case study rather than a claim about institutional adoption.

resources.title: The Default Is Many Chains
resources.tldr: Four thousand words arguing the multi-chain outcome already happened and the question is now how anything coordinates across 170 of them. The strongest statement of that case.

resources.title: Cross-Chain Messaging Explained
resources.tldr: The protocol layer that carries data and instructions between chains, explained from first principles. Start here before reading anything about bridges.

resources.title: Enterprise DVNs: Who Actually Verifies Cross-Chain Messages
resources.tldr: Household-name payment processors and cloud providers now operate verification nodes in production. Read it for how they divide up responsibility for message security.

resources.title: AI-Assisted Security Auditing in the Zcash Ecosystem
resources.tldr: An audit firm reporting honestly on where model assistance helped and where it did not. Rare because the incentive is to claim it works everywhere.

resources.title: Audit of a Legacy Seed Recovery Workspace
resources.tldr: Short, but the subject is unusual: reviewing a tool built to recover old wallet seeds. Recovery tooling has a threat model most audits never encounter.

resources.title: Small Fields: Faster Proving Toward Real-Time Finality
resources.tldr: Cutting proof generation latency and RAM at the same time by changing the field arithmetic. Real cryptographic engineering with a measurable result.

resources.title: Atomic Delivery-Versus-Payment, Settled Privately
resources.tldr: Asset and payment changing hands in one indivisible step across two chains, without publishing who traded what. Built as a proof of concept for regulated settlement.

resources.title: Your Wallet Just Got Smarter Without Changing Your Address
resources.tldr: Adding account abstraction features to an address people already use. The migration problem is usually what stops smart accounts from being adopted.

resources.title: A Beginner's Guide to Trove Management
resources.tldr: Troves are the collateral positions the whole protocol runs on, and mismanaging one is how people get liquidated. Explains what to watch and when to act.

resources.title: A BOLD Stance
resources.tldr: The reasoning behind the stablecoin design rather than the announcement of it. Useful for seeing which trade-offs were chosen deliberately.

resources.title: Addressing Concerns About Liquity
resources.tldr: A protocol answering its critics in detail rather than deflecting. Read it for the objections as much as the responses.

resources.title: Onchain Asset Management in 2025: A Data Review
resources.tldr: Loan volumes, defaults and borrower mix over a full year, published as numbers rather than highlights. Institutional lending is one of the few areas with a real track record now.

resources.title: Bitwise Makes Its First Institutional DeFi Allocation
resources.tldr: An asset manager putting client money into onchain credit, described concretely. More informative about institutional adoption than most surveys of it.

resources.title: Build Your First Aiken Smart Contract
resources.tldr: Writing a Cardano validator in Aiken and then actually locking and unlocking assets with it. Complete enough to run rather than just read.

resources.title: Building a Custom Blockchain Provider
resources.tldr: Implementing the fetcher and submitter interfaces to point an SDK at your own infrastructure. The part of a toolkit that decides whether you can leave it.

resources.title: Minting NFTs on Cardano From Node.js
resources.tldr: Server-side minting with distribution to many recipients. Cardano's UTXO model makes batch operations genuinely different, and this shows how.

resources.title: Threat and Vulnerability Management
resources.tldr: Nobody patches 40,000 CVEs a year, so the real skill is deciding which ones matter to you. Reframes the problem as prioritisation rather than coverage.

resources.title: Preventing SQL Injection: A Developer's Checklist
resources.tldr: Parameterised queries, input validation, least privilege. A decades-old bug class that still ships, laid out as something you can actually work through.

resources.title: Storage for Upgradable Ethereum Smart Contracts
resources.tldr: Upgrade the logic and the storage layout stays behind, which is where upgradeable contracts quietly break. The first part of a series that treats this properly.

resources.title: Collisions of Solidity Storage Layouts
resources.tldr: The follow-up, on what happens when two contracts disagree about which slot holds what. A subtle bug class with expensive consequences.

resources.title: Random Numbers and Decentralized Networks: Implementation
resources.tldr: Long treatment of publicly verifiable random beacons. Randomness that nobody can predict and everybody can check is harder than it sounds, and this shows why.

resources.title: Securing a New Lending Deployment
resources.tldr: The review, monitoring and staged rollout behind a major protocol upgrade. More instructive than an audit report because it covers the process, not the findings.

resources.title: $5B on Base Is the New Day One for Onchain Finance
resources.tldr: A milestone post, but a useful marker of how much credit now sits on a single L2. Read it for the scale rather than the framing.

resources.title: Move 2024 Migration Guide
resources.tldr: Module labels, let mut, public structs, method syntax, enums and match. A language edition changing this much is rare, and the guide is refreshingly direct about breakage.

resources.title: Code Quality Checklist
resources.tldr: A review checklist for Sui contracts covering safety, style and maintainability. Long enough to be genuinely useful rather than a list of platitudes.

resources.title: Upgradeability Practices
resources.tldr: Upgrading a package without breaking whatever depends on it is mostly a planning problem, not a technical one. Covers compatibility and versioning on Sui.

resources.title: How to Create Generative NFT Art Collections for Free
resources.tldr: Generating the artwork, storing it, then deploying the collection without writing code. Complete enough to follow end to end rather than stopping at the fun part.

resources.title: Creating an NFT Project on Monad
resources.tldr: Collection setup, public minting, airdrops and the rest, done on a newer chain. Long and specific, which is what separates a real walkthrough from a summary.

resources.title: NFT Generation Tools Compared
resources.tldr: Seven tools ranked on cost, signup requirements and metadata handling across EVM chains. Vendor-authored, so read the criteria, but the comparison is real.

resources.title: How to Withdraw From Smart Contracts on Etherscan
resources.tldr: Money stuck in a contract you deployed is a common and panicky problem. This walks the block explorer interface that gets it out.

resources.title: Minting NFTs Inside Farcaster Frames, No Code
resources.tldr: Turning a social post into a mint surface, which changed where NFT distribution happens. Worth reading for the mechanic even if you skip the tooling.

resources.title: Turning Telecom Towers Into Secure AI Data Centres
resources.tldr: Existing tower sites hosting private compute at the edge, aggregating into something larger. An unusually physical proposal for a privacy network.

resources.title: Taking Private Health Data Mainstream
resources.tldr: Health apps collect more the closer they get to daily behaviour. Uses that tension to make the case for computing on data you never decrypt.

resources.title: Managed Verification Nodes
resources.tldr: How work gets checked and trusted across a network where no participant can see the data. Short, and central to how the whole model holds together.

resources.title: An $8M Mux-Up: Finding a Critical Vulnerability in MUX Protocol
resources.tldr: Two thousand words tracing a real critical bug from detection to disclosure. The value is in the reasoning path, not the headline figure.

resources.title: Catching a High-Severity Ethereum Client Bug
resources.tldr: A bug in client software rather than a contract, which is a much less examined surface with much broader blast radius.

resources.title: Asymmetric War: Agentic AI and the Future of Cybersecurity
resources.tldr: Attackers and defenders both get the same tooling, and the argument here is about which side the asymmetry favours. Not a comfortable conclusion.

resources.title: The Attack Surface Has Moved to Vault Infrastructure
resources.tldr: A $6M exploit that never touched the contract logic. Vault accounting, stale asset values and strategy adapters are where the real surface now sits.

resources.title: Can ERC-4626 Exploits Be Prevented?
resources.tldr: Uses a live oracle-manipulation exploit on an Aave fork to ask whether the vault standard itself invites this class of bug, or whether the integrators do.

resources.title: Valid Signatures Are Not Enough
resources.tldr: Forty major hacks in a single month, around $647M, and a good number of them were correctly signed transactions. Signature validity says nothing about intent.

resources.title: Tokenized Stocks Backed by DTC Entitlements
resources.tldr: The first tokens backed by entitlements to securities held at the central depository. Unglamorous plumbing, and the part that makes the rest legally real.

resources.title: FINRA Authorizations for Tokenized Equities and Funds
resources.tldr: Regulatory permission to run markets in tokenised securities for US investors. The licence is the hard part; the technology has existed for years.

resources.title: Bringing Japanese Equities On-Chain
resources.tldr: A partnership with one of Japan's largest financial groups. Short, and notable because each new jurisdiction brings its own settlement and custody regime.

resources.title: Over 100 Crypto Projects Shut Down in 2026
resources.tldr: Asks whether the failure rate signals a dot-com style reset rather than a downturn. The count is the argument, and it is worth sitting with.

resources.title: BIP-110 and the Risk of Selling Forked Coins
resources.tldr: A developer warning that claiming coins from a fork can put the original holdings at risk. The replay mechanics catch people out every single time.

resources.title: The AI Agent Economy and On-Chain Settlement
resources.tldr: Reads a major infrastructure company's earnings call as evidence that agent-to-agent payments are arriving. An unusual and fairly persuasive angle.

resources.title: Bringing a BNY High-Yield Bond Fund On-Chain
resources.tldr: Tokenised access to a short-dated high-yield corporate bond strategy from a major custodian. Institutional fixed income is the least glamorous and most consequential RWA category.

resources.title: Settling an OTC Trade in a Yield-Bearing Stablecoin
resources.tldr: Two funds settling with each other using a stablecoin that accrues. Small event, meaningful precedent for what settlement assets can be.

resources.title: Achieving ISO 27001 Certification With Zero Nonconformities
resources.tldr: An independent audit of an information security management system, closed clean. Unexciting and exactly what institutional counterparties ask for.

resources.title: More Than You Ever Wanted to Know About Power Perpetuals
resources.tldr: Six thousand words deriving the pricing from first principles. The title is not a joke, and it is the most complete treatment of these instruments anywhere.

resources.title: Everything Is a Perp
resources.tldr: Assets targeting a power of an index, so ETH squared quadruples when ETH doubles. A genuinely fun rabbit hole once you accept the premise.

resources.title: Variance Perpetuals
resources.tldr: A forward contract on realised variance, made perpetual. Volatility as something you hold a position in rather than something that happens to you.

resources.title: Centaur 2.0: Permissions, Context, and MCP
resources.tldr: A self-hosted multiplayer AI runtime rebuilt around granular permissions. Interesting for how it frames permissioning as the hard part rather than capability.

resources.title: A 30-Day Minimum Holding Period: Community Consultation
resources.tldr: A protocol proposing to restrict its own users to protect liquidity providers, and arguing it in public. Worth reading as governance rather than as product news.

resources.title: P&L Realization Changes and Position Flipping
resources.tldr: Moving to proportional profit realization and blocking rapid flipping. Small mechanical changes that quietly determine which trading strategies remain viable.

resources.title: Getting Started With Real Estate Price Exposure
resources.tldr: Tracking US housing markets with $100 and no tenants, mortgage or paperwork. Short introduction to a genuinely unusual thing to put onchain.

resources.title: What the IPFS Gateway Pivot Means for Businesses
resources.tldr: Public gateways many projects quietly depend on are changing. If your NFTs or app assets resolve through one, this explains what breaks and when.

resources.title: Updating an NFT Image With Hot Swaps
resources.tldr: Making a supposedly immutable image change, and what that reveals about where NFT content really lives. Twenty-six hundred words with working code.

resources.title: Using the IPFS CLI
resources.tldr: Pinning, listing and managing content from the terminal rather than a dashboard. Dull to read and useful the moment you need to script it.

resources.title: Ocash: A Programmable, Privacy-Preserving Settlement Layer
resources.tldr: Private by default, disclosable when required. The design question is who holds the key to that disclosure, and this is where to start on it.

resources.title: From zkML to Privacy Rails: A Year in Review
resources.tldr: Zero-knowledge machine learning, a testnet, and a privacy chain, reviewed together. Useful for seeing how one team's research turned into shipped products.

resources.title: Memory Took the Market: RWA Perp Report
resources.tldr: Record real-world-asset perp volume, with 81% of the increase driven by memory-chip names. A specific, checkable read on what people are actually trading.

resources.title: Asian Equities Coverage Goes Live
resources.tldr: Over a hundred feeds spanning Hong Kong, mainland China, South Korea and Japan. Each market closes at a different hour, which is precisely the difficulty.

resources.title: A Data Business in Public: The July Numbers
resources.tldr: Revenue, conversions and catalogue size, published monthly. Very few crypto projects report commercial metrics this plainly, whatever you make of them.

resources.title: The Exploit Race
resources.tldr: The longest piece here, on the window between an exploit becoming visible and a protocol being able to respond. That window is the whole security problem in one frame.

resources.title: Engineering Smart Contract Families for Solidity
resources.tldr: Designing a set of related contracts as one system rather than several separate ones, and what that changes about upgrades and shared assumptions.

resources.title: Security Beat: Keys Over Code
resources.tldr: The month's incidents, with the observation that keeps recurring: far more value is lost through compromised keys than through flawed contracts.

resources.title: How to Verify a Safe Transaction Before You Sign It
resources.tldr: Your hardware wallet confirms a hash matches; it says nothing about where the funds end up. Sets out what you have to inspect yourself before approving.

resources.title: Safe Modules and Guards: The Hidden Multisig Risk
resources.tldr: A module can move funds without collecting the signatures the multisig was set up to require. Most treasury operators have never audited theirs for this.

resources.title: Prediction Market Security and Oracle Resolution Attacks
resources.tldr: The attack surface is not the trading, it is who decides what happened. As these markets grow, resolution becomes the thing worth attacking.

resources.title: Migrating to RainbowKit and Wagmi v2
resources.tldr: A breaking peer-dependency upgrade laid out change by change. The kind of guide you resent needing and are grateful exists.

resources.title: Upgrading Sign-In With Ethereum to NextAuth v5
resources.tldr: Wiring wallet authentication into a session framework that changed underneath it. Narrow, but it is exactly where SIWE integrations tend to break.

resources.title: Preparing Your dApp for WalletConnect v2
resources.tldr: Short migration notes for the protocol most wallet connections still run through. Worth keeping bookmarked rather than rediscovering mid-outage.

resources.title: Capital Gains Tax on Cryptocurrency in the UK
resources.tldr: Current rates, the annual allowance, and which disposals actually count. Specific to one jurisdiction, which is precisely why it is useful rather than vague.

resources.title: Holding Crypto in a UK Limited Company
resources.tldr: Corporation tax against capital gains tax, setup steps, reporting duties, and honest about when the structure is not worth it.

resources.title: Capital Gains Processes Need to Adapt
resources.tldr: Argues crypto did not create a tax problem so much as expose how badly existing processes handle complexity. Short and more interesting than the title suggests.

resources.title: Release v2.5.3: Circom Frontends and Proof Verification
resources.tldr: Generating a frontend straight from a zero-knowledge circuit, plus onchain proof verification in the IDE. Notable for how far the tooling has moved.

resources.title: Release v2.4.0: AI Security and Gas Audit Checklists
resources.tldr: Structured checklists rather than a chat box, which is a better shape for review work. A good look at where model assistance fits in a dev tool.

resources.title: UX Writing in the Age of AI
resources.tldr: Using models to audit copy rather than generate it. A rare piece that lands on a specific division of labour instead of a position on AI.

resources.title: Optimising an Onchain App to Survive a Bear Market
resources.tldr: Cost structure, retention and what to cut when volume falls. Written for the part of the cycle nobody publishes advice about.

resources.title: Wallet Verification Flows for Compliance: A Case Study
resources.tldr: Connecting wallet authentication to an identity-verification product. Concrete on where the compliance boundary sits in a self-custodial flow.

resources.title: The Self-Driving Company
resources.tldr: Code output nearly tripled in six months while review times and incident rates held. Whether you believe the numbers, the operational detail is worth reading.

resources.title: Evaluating and Improving an Agent at Scale
resources.tldr: Users arrive with a goal in natural language and no repo, tests or framework. How do you measure whether the agent did well? Twenty-six hundred words on that problem.

resources.title: AI Adoption Starts With Truth
resources.tldr: One confidently wrong answer and a user stops trusting the tool entirely. Makes the case that a reliable data layer is the prerequisite, not the polish.

resources.title: Postmortem: The March 2026 Incident
resources.tldr: Twenty-two hundred words on what broke and why, published rather than summarised. Incident writing is the fastest way to learn how a protocol really works.

resources.title: The Path Forward
resources.tldr: Five thousand words setting out where a synthetic dollar protocol goes next. Long enough to actually contain the reasoning rather than the conclusions.

resources.title: Integrating a AAA CLO Fund
resources.tldr: Bringing collateralised loan obligations into a crypto-backed dollar product. Worth reading closely for how the risk of that asset class is being handled.

resources.title: A Guide to Liquid Staking and Restaking
resources.tldr: TVL went from roughly $14B to $85B in about a year, and this walks through how the protocols behind that differ. Comparative rather than promotional.

resources.title: Staking Bitcoin With Babylon to Secure Proof-of-Stake Networks
resources.tldr: Using idle BTC as economic security for other chains, without moving it. One of the more genuinely novel primitives of that period.

resources.title: How to Make Money as an Ethereum Validator
resources.tldr: Where validator income actually comes from, what erodes it, and the operational costs people forget. Blunt about the margins.

resources.title: What Is Silk?
resources.tldr: A privacy-preserving stablecoin pegged to a basket rather than to the dollar alone. Explains why the basket design was chosen and what it trades away.

resources.title: ShadeX: Redefining Lending and Borrowing via Encryption
resources.tldr: Public lending markets expose every position to anyone watching. Works through what changes when balances are encrypted by default.

resources.title: Introducing Feather
resources.tldr: Governance participation usually demands attention nobody has. Describes delegating that without handing over the underlying assets.

resources.title: Price Oracle Manipulation in Smart Contracts
resources.tldr: Move the price the contract reads and you move everything downstream of it. Still one of the most productive attack classes in DeFi.

resources.title: What Is the Entropy Illusion Vulnerability?
resources.tldr: Randomness that looks unpredictable and is not. A narrower bug class than reentrancy and considerably less well understood.

resources.title: ISO 20022 and What It Means for Blockchain
resources.tldr: The messaging standard the banking system is migrating to, and where onchain settlement would have to meet it. Dry subject, real consequences.

resources.title: MiCAR and BaFin Compliance in Plain English
resources.tldr: What the European regime changes for stablecoins and token launches, with timelines and the pitfalls teams keep hitting. Readable without a legal background.

resources.title: Digital Asset Risk Assessments for Custodians and Exchanges
resources.tldr: Runs from contract-level review through to operational process, which is the half institutions usually discover they were missing.

resources.title: Trust Levels
resources.tldr: How a community grades the weight of its own members' contributions. The core idea behind reputation-weighted rewards, in a few hundred words.

resources.title: Boosting
resources.tldr: Staking earned rewards behind work you want to see happen. An unusual mechanism: it turns reputation into a signal about the future rather than the past.

resources.title: Initiatives
resources.tldr: The unit for describing efforts too large to be one contribution. Short, and the piece that makes the rest of the model coherent.

resources.title: 17 Real-World Use Cases for Blockchain Technology
resources.tldr: Three thousand words of concrete applications rather than categories. Long lists are usually filler; this one holds up because each case is specific.

resources.title: AI Agents Need Data Before They Can Transact
resources.tldr: An agent that cannot verify what it is looking at cannot safely act on it. Frames verifiable data as the prerequisite rather than an enhancement.

resources.title: Activity-Based Rewards Instead of Yield
resources.tldr: Paying for what people do rather than for what they lock up. Short, and a useful counterpoint to the standard incentive design.

resources.title: Why Stablecoins Will Power America's Next Fintech Giant
resources.tldr: Argues the constraint on new fintechs has always been bank partnerships and settlement cost, and that both loosen once the rail is a stablecoin rather than ACH.

resources.title: How Stablecoins Will Change Business Banking
resources.tldr: Instant account setup, programmable rules and yield on the balance are things a business bank account has never offered. Sets out what that competition looks like.

resources.title: Embedded Finance's Missing Piece
resources.tldr: Embedding payments into a platform is solved; embedding settlement is not. On why real-time settlement is the piece that has been missing from embedded finance.

resources.title: Fuzzing Made Easy: How to Decide What to Fuzz
resources.tldr: Choosing the target is harder than writing the harness, and choosing badly burns weeks of compute for nothing. Picks a surface by following untrusted input to where it lands.

resources.title: Fuzzing Made Easy: How to Perform Coverage Analysis
resources.tldr: Over ten thousand words on finding the code your campaign never reached and adjusting it accordingly. Without this step a fuzzer can run for weeks and prove nothing.

resources.title: OpenVPN 2.7 Security Audit: 18 Findings and What Made the Difference
resources.tldr: A sixteen-week audit of a release candidate, written up with the reasoning intact. The section on what actually surfaced the critical bug is the valuable part.

resources.title: Understanding the Quantum Threat
resources.tldr: Not everything on a chain is equally exposed, and this locates the parts that genuinely are. Equally frank about what moving off them would cost.

resources.title: Formal Verification of the STRK20 Privacy Pool
resources.tldr: A privacy protocol verified in Lean with over 230 machine-checked proofs. Formal verification at this scale on a shipped protocol is still rare.

resources.title: STARKs and Native Account Abstraction as Quantum Defence
resources.tldr: What actually makes a cryptocurrency quantum-resistant, argued across two layers: the proof system and how accounts authorise anything at all.

resources.title: Curve CryptoPool With Donations
resources.tldr: Fourteen thousand words taking one AMM design apart to the arithmetic. If you have ever wanted to genuinely understand a Curve pool rather than use one, this is the piece.

resources.title: How YieldBasis Really Works
resources.tldr: Ten thousand words on a protocol most coverage describes in a paragraph. The word really in the title is earned.

resources.title: Fixed-Rate Lending in DeFi: A Design Review
resources.tldr: Notional, TermMax and Pendle solving the same yield-uncertainty problem three different ways, compared at the architecture level rather than the marketing one.

resources.title: Q1 2026 Transparency Report
resources.tldr: Twenty-four hundred words of spending, tokenomics and governance decisions, published quarterly. Very few projects open their books like this.

resources.title: Q4 2025 Transparency Report
resources.tldr: The previous quarter, covering the pivot toward many-to-many video. Reading two of these in sequence tells you more than any roadmap would.

resources.title: Network Security Incident: Full Disclosure and Recovery Plan
resources.tldr: Root cause, timeline and a commitment to make every affected staker whole. Published fast and without hedging, which is the standard others should be held to.

resources.title: How OpenZeppelin Handles Access Control Across 30+ Chains
resources.tldr: A real architecture walkthrough of running multi-chain data with no backend of your own. The constraint is what makes it interesting.

resources.title: Multi-Chain Perpetual Futures Indexing: A Case Study
resources.tldr: Perps generate a punishing volume of events, and indexing them across chains is where most data layers fall over. This shows what held.

resources.title: Security Incident Report: Hedera Pull-Oracle Verifier
resources.tldr: An attacker found a cryptographic edge case in an on-chain verifier. Published with the timeline and the specific flaw, which is more than most incidents get.

resources.title: Hydrangea++: Consensus With Optimistic Proposals
resources.tldr: Pushing block latency toward its theoretical floor by assuming the happy path and recovering when wrong. Real consensus engineering, written for people who want the detail.

resources.title: Parallel EVM Execution Compared
resources.tldr: A benchmark against a competitor with an open challenge to disprove it. Read it for the methodology argument as much as the numbers.

resources.title: The Next Oracle Problem Is Not Price
resources.tldr: Price feeds are the solved part. Argues the harder question is verifying everything else an onchain system needs to know, especially once AI-generated noise enters the inputs.

resources.title: Verifiable Off-Chain Execution in the AI Era
resources.tldr: If the computation happens off-chain, the chain is trusting a claim about it. Makes the case for proving that work rather than attesting to it.

resources.title: 501 Sources of Real-World Yield and How to Bring Them On-Chain
resources.tldr: An actual inventory rather than a category argument. The count itself is the useful part, and so is what each source needs before it can be referenced onchain.

resources.title: What Is Taiko?
resources.tldr: Based sequencing explained at length: what it means to hand block ordering back to Ethereum's own proposers, and what that buys you.

resources.title: ERC-8004: The Trustless Agent Standard
resources.tldr: How an autonomous agent registers an onchain identity others can verify. An emerging standard worth understanding before it becomes assumed knowledge.

resources.title: Deploying AI Agents On-Chain
resources.tldr: The practical side: fees low enough that an agent can transact freely, and sequencing that cannot quietly exclude it. Both matter more than they sound.

resources.title: What Is a Threshold Signature Wallet?
resources.tldr: Splitting a single key so no party ever holds it whole, and honest about the drawbacks alongside the security gain. Twenty-four hundred words, balanced.

resources.title: How Threshold Signatures Actually Work
resources.tldr: The cryptography underneath, at a level you can follow without a maths degree. Read after the overview if you want to know why it holds.

resources.title: How Multisig Wallets Work: Strengths and Weaknesses
resources.tldr: Bitcoin and Ethereum multisig compared, including what each one leaks and what it costs. Multisig and threshold signatures solve overlapping but different problems.

resources.title: Building Secure Uniswap v4 Hooks
resources.tldr: Hooks let anyone inject logic into a pool, which is the whole point and also why they break. Catalogues the mistakes that keep reappearing in shipped hook code.

resources.title: A Few Notes on AWS Nitro Enclaves and KMS Integration
resources.tldr: Very long and very specific on the risks of wiring an enclave to a key management service. Relevant to anyone putting signing keys inside a TEE.

resources.title: Mutation Testing Comes to DAML
resources.tldr: Mutation testing deliberately breaks your code to find out whether the test suite notices. The clearest way to learn that coverage and rigour are not the same thing.

resources.title: Self-Hosting Solana History: Run Your Own Archive RPC
resources.tldr: Four thousand words of ClickHouse setup, schema and live ingestion. If you have ever wondered what a history node actually costs to operate, this answers it.

resources.title: Inside Cloudbreak: Indexing Architecture for Account Reads
resources.tldr: Half a billion accounts served fast enough to feel like an ordinary database query. The engineering interest is in which storage engine they settled on and why.

resources.title: Backfilling Solana History Step by Step
resources.tldr: Reconstructing the chain's past from archives rather than replaying it. Tedious, necessary, and almost never documented at this level of detail.

resources.title: An Agent Kit for Non-Custodial Wallets
resources.tldr: Letting an AI agent hold value and pay for things without handing custody to a service. The permission design is the hard part and this engages with it.

resources.title: Putting an Assistant Inside a Wallet
resources.tldr: Reading a portfolio and assembling transactions through conversation. Interesting mostly for where the product draws the line on what it will execute.

resources.title: A Hardware Wallet Is Not Enough: Behind the NFT God Hack
resources.tldr: A cold wallet protects the key and does nothing about what you agree to sign. Uses a well-known theft to show how the device was never the weak point.

resources.title: Address Poisoning Is Accelerating: What the Data Shows
resources.tldr: Measures the attack rather than describing it, which makes the scale clear. The mechanism preys on people checking only the first and last characters of an address.

resources.title: Agent Payment Security: The Asset Layer Nobody Is Checking
resources.tldr: Most agent-payment discussion stops at spending limits. Argues the unexamined risk is what the agent is being paid in, and whether that asset is what it claims.

resources.title: Providing Liquidity on Uniswap With an AI Agent
resources.tldr: Handing an LP position to Claude or Codex through a CLI. Worth reading for what it implies about who is executing DeFi transactions soon.

resources.title: An Agent That Sweeps, Sorts and Consolidates a Portfolio
resources.tldr: Dust cleanup and consolidation are exactly the tedious jobs worth automating first. A grounded example of agent tooling rather than a demo.

resources.title: Trading Tokenized Stocks From a Self-Custodial Wallet
resources.tldr: Six hundred equities as tokens, traded without an intermediary holding them. The custody question is the interesting one here, not the ticker list.

resources.title: The DeFi Death Spiral: Business Model Failures Behind Crypto's Biggest Collapses
resources.tldr: Traces several famous blowups back to the economics rather than the exploit. The pattern that emerges is that the model was unsustainable long before it broke.

resources.title: How an AI-Powered Rollup Approaches Security
resources.tldr: Screening transactions at the sequencer before they are included, rather than reacting once they land. A genuinely different position in the stack to intervene from.

resources.title: A New Chapter: From L2 to DeFi
resources.tldr: A chain announcing it is repositioning as a DeFi product. Short, but a candid example of how infrastructure teams end up moving up the stack.
